doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Sweet and Low Down: Howard Alden and the script
summary: Hyman discusses the Woody Allen film, Howard Alden's playing and Sean Penn miming, and characters like Emmett Ray.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well I’d like to talk about a couple of things. First of all I recently saw the latest Woody Allen film and I thought that was a great piece of work.

Well thank you. Everybody has enjoyed that film and paid more attention to it really than some of the earlier ones in which I worked far harder. There’s a lot more to do on “Everyone Says I Love You,” than on this one. This one was mostly Howard, Howard Alden. He did a marvelous job. And mainly these things were pre-recorded and Howard taught Sean Penn to mime his playing very well. And so this had very few of the problems that you usually have of putting music in afterwards. It’s easier if you do it in front and the film adapts to what you did.
I see. We should — for people who might watch this — we should say we’re talking about “Sweet and Low Down.”
Yeah. Did you like the script?
I thought it was very funny and strangely true to life. I’ve known several people like this. I’ve known guys who reminded me strongly of that Emmett Ray, and I’d better not name them.
